name: Direct crude cracking
principle: Crude oil, or a light fraction of it, is sent directly to a steam cracker to make olefins and aromatics, skipping some or all of the conventional distillation and conversion steps. ExxonMobil's Singapore cracker started up in 2013 as the first to process crude directly. Saudi Aramco, Lummus and Chevron Lummus Global developed TC2C, which uses steam dilution to vaporise a light cut for the cracker, hydroprocesses a heart cut, and converts the heaviest fraction in liquid-circulation reactors.

performance.metric: slurry hydrocracking residue conversion in TC2C
performance.basis: more than 97% of residue; LC reactors can run more than five years

source.note: PTQ / Digital Refining, Crude to chemicals Part 2 (Saudi Aramco TC2C)

performance.metric: TC2C (thermal crude-to-chemicals) chemicals yield from crude
performance.unit: % of feed crude converted to chemicals (S&P Global: '70% (or higher) possible'; Aramco/SABIC stated target 70-80%; pilot results reported exceeding 70%)
performance.basis: TC2C direct crude cracking (Saudi Aramco/Lummus): highest chemicals yield from crude, >70%, with about 30-40% lower CAPEX than conventional refinery/ethylene integration (Lummus-Aramco TC2C paper, PTQ/digitalrefining); ExxonMobil crude-cracking yield figure not published in open sources
